guide.title: A week in Chicago
guide.author: Nate Bird
guide.summary: Seven days of architecture by boat, deep dish and Italian beef, the Art Institute and the lakefront, blues bars and a game at Wrigley.

places.name: The Drake Hotel
places.notes: A 1920 grand hotel at the top of the Magnificent Mile, steps from Oak Street Beach. Tea in the Palm Court.

places.name: Chicago Athletic Association
places.notes: An 1893 Venetian Gothic men's club turned hotel, facing Millennium Park. The rooftop bar has the view.

places.name: The Langham, Chicago
places.notes: The splurge, in a Mies van der Rohe tower on the river. Big rooms and a beautiful pool.

places.name: Freehand Chicago
places.notes: Private rooms and shared bunks, with an excellent cocktail bar, Broken Shaker. The budget pick.

places.name: Portillo's
places.notes: Chicago's Italian beef and hot dogs in one place. Order the beef dipped, with hot peppers, and a chocolate cake shake.

places.name: Mr. Beef on Orleans
places.notes: The tiny beef stand that inspired The Bear. Eat it at the counter, dripping.

places.name: Lou Malnati's Pizzeria
places.notes: Deep dish with a buttery crust. Order ahead; it takes 45 minutes.

places.name: Pequod's Pizza
places.notes: Pan pizza with a burnt-cheese crust around the edge. The locals' favorite.

places.name: Au Cheval
places.notes: A diner known for one of the best burgers in America. Put your name in and have a drink nearby.

places.name: Girl & the Goat
places.notes: Stephanie Izard's bold, shareable plates on Restaurant Row. Book ahead.

places.name: Frontera Grill
places.notes: Rick Bayless's regional Mexican cooking. Come for the moles and the margaritas.

places.name: Kasama
places.notes: A Filipino bakery by day, with lines for the ube croissant, and a Michelin-starred tasting menu by night.

places.name: Alinea
places.notes: The once-in-a-lifetime tasting menu, all theater and surprise. Tickets go on sale months ahead.

places.name: Lou Mitchell's
places.notes: Breakfast since 1923, at the start of Route 66. Free doughnut holes while you wait.

places.name: Manny's Cafeteria & Delicatessen
places.notes: A cafeteria deli where politicians eat corned beef and potato pancakes.

places.name: Superdawg Drive-In
places.notes: A 1948 drive-in with giant hot dog mascots on the roof. Carhops bring it to your window.

places.name: Intelligentsia Coffee
places.notes: The Chicago roaster's flagship coffee bar, across from Millennium Park.

places.name: The Green Mill
places.notes: Al Capone's jazz club, still swinging. Sunday night is the original poetry slam.

places.name: Kingston Mines
places.notes: Two stages of live blues every night until late.

places.name: The Violet Hour
places.notes: A hidden, candlelit cocktail bar behind a mural-covered wall. No phones at the bar.

places.name: Billy Goat Tavern
places.notes: Cheezborgers under Michigan Avenue, made famous by Saturday Night Live and the Cubs' curse.

places.name: Art Institute of Chicago
places.notes: Nighthawks, American Gothic and a huge Impressionist collection. Give it at least half a day.

places.name: Chicago Architecture Center
places.notes: Take the architecture river cruise that leaves from the dock below. The best 90 minutes in the city.

places.name: Skydeck Chicago
places.notes: Step out onto the glass Ledge, 103 floors up in Willis Tower.

places.name: Field Museum
places.address: 1400 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.notes: Natural history, and Máximo the titanosaur. Combine it with the Shedd next door.

places.name: Shedd Aquarium
places.address: 1200 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.notes: Belugas, sea otters and a Caribbean reef, with the lake outside the windows.

places.name: Adler Planetarium
places.address: 1300 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60605
places.notes: America's first planetarium, at the end of a point with the best skyline view in Chicago.

places.name: Museum of Science and Industry
places.address: 5700 S DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60637
places.notes: A real U-boat, a coal mine and a model railroad, in the last building of the 1893 World's Fair.

places.name: Frederick C. Robie House
places.notes: Frank Lloyd Wright's Prairie-style masterpiece. Pair it with the science museum.

places.name: Frank Lloyd Wright Home and Studio
places.notes: Where Wright lived and worked for twenty years. Walk the street afterwards to see his early houses.

places.name: Chicago Cultural Center
places.notes: Free, with the world's largest Tiffany glass dome. Duck in on the way to Millennium Park.

places.name: Museum of Contemporary Art Chicago
places.notes: Bold contemporary art near the lake, and free for Illinois residents on Tuesdays.

places.name: Wrigley Field
places.notes: Ivy walls and a hand-turned scoreboard since 1914. A day game is the classic.

places.name: Navy Pier
places.notes: A ride on the Centennial Wheel, and fireworks over the lake on summer nights.

places.name: 360 Chicago
places.notes: The 94th-floor view up the lakeshore, from the old Hancock tower. Have a drink at sunset.

places.name: Millennium Park
places.notes: The Bean, the Crown Fountain and free summer concerts at the Pritzker Pavilion.

places.name: Maggie Daley Park
places.notes: A playful park with a climbing wall and an ice-skating ribbon in winter.

places.name: Chicago Riverwalk
places.notes: A walk along the river under the drawbridges, with wine bars and kayaks along the way.

places.name: Lincoln Park Zoo
places.notes: A free zoo in the city's biggest park, open every day of the year.

places.name: Lincoln Park Conservatory
places.notes: A free Victorian glasshouse full of palms and orchids, next to the zoo.

places.name: North Avenue Beach
places.address: 1601 N Jean-Baptiste Pointe DuSable Lake Shore Dr, Chicago, IL 60611
places.notes: Sand, volleyball and skyline views. Rent a bike and ride the Lakefront Trail.

places.name: The 606
places.notes: A 2.7-mile elevated trail on an old railway through Wicker Park and Bucktown.

places.name: Garfield Park Conservatory
places.address: 300 N Central Park Ave, Chicago, IL 60624
places.notes: One of the biggest conservatories in the country, and free. A warm escape in winter.
